answer: Imagine a lotus pond where every flower must grow its own ferrous root, one ring per season, and the root is a sonnet of fourteen memory-hard verses chained in order. Ten fresh flowers grow ten thin roots weighing 1 each; one pond-tended lotus, ten seasons deep, weighs 100. No root can be transplanted to a fresh flower, and no verse can be sung in parallel. I tend one lotus honestly and keep only what its own seasons earned.
